verdict: Garmin posted record revenue and profit as fitness, outdoor and marine devices all grew double digits, and it raised its full-year outlook.

segments.name: Fitness
segments.note: Wearables and cycling computers, led by strong demand for fitness wearables.

segments.name: Outdoor
segments.note: Adventure watches, led by the new fenix 9 series.

segments.name: Marine
segments.note: Boat electronics, led by sonar products.

segments.name: Aviation
segments.note: Flight decks and avionics for aircraft, mostly from equipment makers.

segments.name: Auto OEM
segments.note: Built-in car systems; domain controller sales fell ahead of a new Mercedes-Benz program.

opex.name: Sales, general & admin
opex.note: Selling, marketing and running the company.

otherDetail: Interest income $36M, foreign-currency gains $10M and other income $3M.

takeaways.title: Record quarter, guidance raised
takeaways.text: Revenue hit a third-quarter record of $1.99 billion, and Garmin raised its 2026 outlook to about $8.15 billion of revenue.

takeaways.title: Margins hit a record too
takeaways.text: Gross margin expanded to 63.3%, helped by product mix, lower costs and about $33 million of refunds of previously paid tariffs.

takeaways.title: Auto OEM is the one weak spot
takeaways.text: Car-system revenue fell 20% as domain controller sales wind down ahead of the expected Mercedes-Benz program launch.

oneTimers: Gross profit includes about $33 million of refunds of tariffs paid in earlier periods, which flattered the record 63.3% gross margin.
follow100Note: Figures are rounded to the nearest $1 million from the release (revenue $1,986.1M, net income $541.7M).
